name: Pale Soft Blue-Violet
lede: Pale Soft Blue-Violet is a light, muted blue-violet, the pale tone Robert Ridgway charted beside the parent color Soft Blue-Violet in his 1912 color atlas.

sections.title: A pale tone of Soft Blue-Violet
sections.body:
Pale Soft Blue-Violet stacks two of Ridgway's own words, Pale and Soft, onto the base hue [[blue-violet]], naming [[soft-blue-violet]] as its direct parent [1]. Soft Blue-Violet is Ridgway's plate XXIII, hue 55 prime, later filed by the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 in block 206 [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[periwinkle]], 2.8 units off and more vivid than this swatch [1]; [[pale-greyish-violet-blue]] sits 3.6 units away, reading duller and bluer [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in only 11 of 23,781 paintings, 0.05 percent, as photographed; narrowing to at least five percent coverage inside a painting leaves 8, rarer than 70 percent of the named colors in our library [2]. It peaks in the 1800s, present in 0.1 percent of the 8,345 paintings from that century, 1.8 times the archive's overall rate [2].

The earliest match dates to 1484, in a work by Pietro Perugino, a floor and not a first since the archive's early centuries are thin; that is 428 years before the name's 1912 record, so the match marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a surviving pigment [2].
